h: The engineer behind the bridge, and where to go next
p: That bouncy bridge has a famous name behind it. It was put up in the 1870s by Sir John Fowler, the Victorian engineer who owned the Braemore estate and who later went on to co-design the Forth Bridge. It's a nice thought as you edge across: the same mind that dreamed up one of Scotland's most famous bridges was also busy with this little one high above the Droma.

The numbers are impressive too. The gorge runs for over a kilometre and drops to around sixty metres deep in places, and the Falls of Measach plunge a long way down into it. After heavy rain the roar is something else, so a wet day can actually be the best time to see it, as long as you've got your waterproofs on.

Most people spend about an hour here, which is just right as a break on a long drive. If you're tackling the North Coast 500, Ullapool sits right on the route, and this is a perfect stop on the way in.

Ullapool itself was founded in 1788 as a herring port, and its neat grid of streets still shows that planned beginning. From the harbour, CalMac ferries sail to Stornoway on the Isle of Lewis, and boat trips head out to the Summer Isles in the warmer months.

Head the other way along the A832 and you'll reach Inverewe Garden at Poolewe, where subtropical plants thrive thanks to the Gulf Stream. North of Ullapool, Knockan Crag is a fascinating stop for anyone interested in how the Highlands were formed.
